short: The lead ship of her class and the heaviest battleship ever constructed, Yamato embodied the pinnacle of Japanese naval gunnery.
full:
Commissioned shortly after the attack on Pearl Harbor in late 1941, Yamato was armed with unprecedented 18.1-inch main guns. Designed to counter the numerical superiority of the US Navy, she served as the flagship of the Combined Fleet. Despite her immense firepower, she spent most of the war sheltered in port as naval warfare shifted decisively toward aircraft carriers.

Yamato fired her main guns at enemy surface targets only once, during the Battle off Samar in October 1944. In April 1945, she was dispatched on a one-way mission to Okinawa to fight until destroyed. Intercepted by American carrier aircraft, Yamato was overwhelmed by bombs and torpedoes, sinking with most of her crew and marking the definitive end of the battleship era.
